name: Ishmael
overview: Ishmael, a male figure mentioned in 2 Kings 25:23, is identified as the son of Nethaniah, a captain of Judean forces during the Babylonian captivity. There is no recorded tribe or additional notes associated with this Ishmael in the biblical text provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Ishmael means 'G-d [El] he heard,' reflecting a recognition of God's attention. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God according to the scripture reference in 2 Kings 25:23.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ishmael as the son of Nethaniah, linking him to a family involved in leadership during a critical period of Judah's history. No other family relationships are noted for this Ishmael beyond his father.
scriptureSignificance: This Ishmael is significant as a descendant of Nethaniah, who held a military leadership role during the Babylonian captivity, a pivotal moment for the Judean people. While distinct from the earlier Ishmael, son of Abraham, this Ishmael's mention ties him to the historical narrative of Judah's exile and restoration challenges. His presence in the text underscores the ongoing leadership and struggles of God's people in a time of national crisis.
